title: Traffic Orbit Anchoring and Lifecycle Choreography for Cohort-sticky A/B + Shadow Rehearsals
author: Priya Patel
description: Context: Large staged rollouts have brittle stickiness semantics when users move between cohorts, and our existing promote/rollback primitives produce noisy telemetry during shadow rehearsals. This PR introduces 'Traffic Orbit Anchoring' — a lightweight, deterministic anchor that binds a user/session fingerprint to an orbit (control/variant/shadow-rehearse) and a lifecycle ledger that records ephemeral rehearsal snapshots for reproducible rollback. Motivation: reduce flakiness in A/B experiments and make automated rollback decisions reproducible across replays and dry-runs. What this change does: 1) Adds an orbit assignment layer implemented as a hash-space anchor that respects sticky cohorts, TTLs, and manual overrides. 2) Introduces a compact lifecycle ledger (immutable snapshot metadata; references to model revision, quantization profile, and rollout policy) that is emitted at cutover and used by the rollback oracle to replay state. 3) Extends the shadow rehearse flow to emit dry-run diffs against the ledger so that post-mortem reproductions are deterministic. 4) Adds metric gating on multi-dimensional SLOs (latency P95, error-rate, and semantic-flip-rate) with configurable thresholds and hysteresis to avoid flip-flop. 5) Implements a safe-commit protocol for final promote that validates ledger consistency and model binary checksum before atomic swap. Backwards compatibility: Orbit anchoring uses feature flag rollouts; if disabled, default behavior is our previous sampler. Rollout plan: feature-flag on for internal canaries for 48 hours, rollout to beta orgs, then general availability. Testing: unit tests + integration harness with synthetic cohort churn and a canary run in benchmark-lab with production-like traffic shape. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear: ENG-4219) - [x] Unit tests for anchor assignment - [x] Integration test for ledger replay - [x] End-to-end dry-run validation in bench environment - [x] Console metrics and tracing hooks added - [x] Feature flag with per-org opt-in Known limitations: Replay requires consistent prompt hashing; semantic-flip-rate is best-effort and may need model-specific normalization. Related work items: ENG-4219, ENG-4333, PM-88. Merge notes: squash-merge to keep ledger history compact.

review_comments: Eve Lin: Nice design. Two questions: how do we keep ledger size bounded for long-lived customers? Also: need a migration path for existing in-flight rollouts.

Priya Patel: Ledger stores metadata only (refs, checksums) and uses retention policy per-org; added retention config and garbage-collection hook. For in-flight rollouts we consult the feature-flag and fallback to sampler semantics; added details to the doc.
Marco Alvarez: Gate thresholds look reasonable; can we make semantic-flip-rate opt-in per-model to avoid noisy signals on non-deterministic models?
Priya Patel: Added per-model gating config with default off; included permissive rollout in tests.
